title: "1 · The PPP action and driver"
subtitle: "`PPP_Interaction.tpp`, `PPP_GaugeAction.tpp`, `hubbardFermiAction.tpp`, `autotune_RadialMCMC_PPP`"

## Model and decoupling

$$
H = -\sum_{xy,\sigma}\kappa_{xy}\,c^\dagger_{x\sigma}c_{y\sigma}
  + \frac12\sum_{xy}V_{xy}\,q_xq_y ,\qquad
q_x = n_{x\uparrow}+n_{x\downarrow}-1,\quad V_{xx}=U
$$

On every time slice, for symmetric positive-definite $V$:

$$
e^{-\delta H_V}\;\propto\;\int d\phi_t\; e^{-\frac12\phi_t^T(\delta V)^{-1}\phi_t\;+\;i\,\phi_t\cdot q}
$$

- The $q_x$ commute with each other, so the Gaussian identity holds for the operators. The only approximation
  is the Trotter split of $e^{-\delta H}$ into kinetic and interaction factors.
- Gauge action $S_g[\phi]=\frac12\sum_t\phi_t^T(\delta V)^{-1}\phi_t$. The field couples as $e^{\pm i\phi}$,
  i.e. through the **charge-basis** fermion matrix `HubbardExp`.
- $V=U\,\mathbb 1$ gives `HubbardGaugeAction` exactly (unit test).
- The integral exists only for $V>0$. The PPP matrices here are positive definite (perylene:
  $\lambda(V)=0.87\ldots20.7\,t$); the action now refuses any other $V$.

## The original `PPPGaugeAction` (last commit, abridged)

```cpp
PPPGaugeAction(double **positions, NSL::Parameter & params) :
    ...
    Utilde_(NSL::Hubbard::tilde<Type>(params,"U")),     // δU: correct
    U_(params["U"].template to<NSL::size_t>())           // U read as an integer
{
    for (int i=0;i<Nx_;i++) for (int j=0;j<Nx_;j++) {
        R = |r_i - r_j|;                                 // units of a
        invVtilde_(i,j) = Utilde_/(1+U_*R*t1_*a_/e2_);   // Mataga–Nishimoto, ε = 1
    }
    invVtilde_ = NSL::LinAlg::mat_inv(invVtilde_);
}
// eval/force/grad: loop over t, invVtildePhi_(t,...) = mat_vec(invVtilde_, phi(t,...)); grad returns invVtildePhi_
```

- **Bug:** `U_` is a `size_t` conversion. $U=3.33$ entered the off-diagonal elements as 3 (deck 5, A1).
- **Bug:** `grad()` returned the member buffer `invVtildePhi_`, which the next call overwrites (deck 5, A2).
- Hard-coded Mataga–Nishimoto with $t=2.7$ eV, $a=1.4$ Å, no dielectric screening; positions as `double**`.
- CPU only (fails with `--GPU`); $N_t$ matrix–vector products per call; no check that $V>0$.
- Nothing instantiated it. The production driver used the spin basis, which cannot work (deck 2).

## The new structure

```text
yml:  PPP: {form, hopping energy, length unit, dielectric}     system: {U, positions}
        │
        ▼  NSL::PPP::interactionMatrixFromYAML                     (PPP_Interaction.tpp)
V  (Nx × Nx, units of t, V_xx = U)
        │
        ▼  PPPGaugeAction(V, params)                               (PPP_GaugeAction.tpp)
checks: square, matches Nx, symmetric, positive definite   → std::invalid_argument otherwise
eigh(V) once, in double precision on the CPU  →  δV, (δV)^-1, (δV)^1/2  moved to params["device"]
        │
        ├─ eval / force / grad : one matmul each, fresh tensors
        ├─ sample(phi)         : phi_t ~ N(0, δV), the initial field of the driver
        └─ Vtilde(), invVtilde(), lambdaMin(), lambdaMax()   (used by exact Fourier acceleration)
```

```cpp
// S = ½ Σ_t φ_t (δV)^{-1} φ_t ,  phi has shape (Nt, Nx), V symmetric
return (phi * NSL::LinAlg::mat_mul(phi, invVtilde_)).sum() / 2.;                          // eval
return Configuration<TensorType>{{this->configKey_, -NSL::LinAlg::mat_mul(phi, invVtilde_)}}; // force
```

The second constructor `PPPGaugeAction(const YAML::Node &, params)` reads $V$ directly from the yml file.

## Interaction forms

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```yaml
PPP:
  form: ohno           # ohno | mataga-nishimoto
                       # | onsite | explicit
  hopping energy: 2.4  # t in eV    (default 2.7)
  length unit: 1.4     # Å per position unit
  dielectric: 2.0      # ε for x ≠ y (default 1)
  # e2: 14.399645      # e²/4πε₀ in eV Å
  # V: [[...], ...]    # explicit form only
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
| form | $V_{xy}$, $x\ne y$ |
|---|---|
| `ohno` | $U\big/\sqrt{1+(U\epsilon r/e^2)^2}$ |
| `mataga-nishimoto` | $U\big/(1+U\epsilon r/e^2)$ |
| `onsite` | $0$ (Hubbard) |
| `explicit` | given matrix |

$r$ in Å and $U$ in eV inside the formulas; the result is converted back to units of $t$.
Both forms approach $e^2/(\epsilon r)$ at large $r$.
:::
::::

- `U` stays in `system: U` (units of $t$), as for the Hubbard runs.
- `ppp_ed.py` and the other Python tools read the same block, so NSL and ED always use the same $V$
  (checked: $|V_\text{NSL}-V_\text{python}|\le 2\cdot10^{-16}$).

## Why screened Ohno for the benchmarks

You asked for the parameter set best suited to the benchmarks, with the forms kept switchable.
Screened Ohno, $t=2.4$ eV, $U=8$ eV, $\epsilon=2$, bond 1.4 Å:

- A standard set for π-conjugated hydrocarbons.
- The long-range part is strong: nearest-neighbour $V\approx0.54\,U$. A benchmark only tests the PPP
  implementation if the off-diagonal $V_{xy}$ matter, and here they do: the same NSL data compared with
  on-site-only ED give $\langle z^2\rangle\approx400$–$650$ (deck 3).
- $V$ is well conditioned (condition number ≈ 10–24 from benzene to perylene), so the HMC stays efficient.
  The remaining stiffness is removed by exact Fourier acceleration (deck 4).

Any other form or parameter set is one change in the yml file.

## Choosing the basis at compile time

**Before** (`hubbardFermiAction.tpp`), a runtime string comparison:

```cpp
if (!hfm_.basis.compare("CHARGE")) { hfm_.populate(phi, NSL::Hubbard::Species::Particle); ... }
else                               { hfm_.populate(phi, NSL::Hubbard::Spin::Up);          ... }
```

Both branches are compiled for every fermion matrix. `Species` and `Spin` are plain enums, so the branch
that does not fit the matrix still compiled: the enum converted to the `bool reshape` argument of
`populate(phi, bool)`. The same silent conversion produced a wrong measurement in `propagator.cpp`
(deck 5, A3).

**After:**

```cpp
template<typename M, typename T>
concept ChargeBasis = requires(M m, const NSL::Tensor<T> & phi) { m.populate(phi, NSL::Hubbard::Species::Particle); };

if constexpr (NSL::FermionMatrix::ChargeBasis<FermionMatrixType,Type>) { /* particles, holes */ }
else { static_assert(NSL::FermionMatrix::SpinBasis<FermionMatrixType,Type>, "..."); /* spin up, spin down */ }

template<std::same_as<bool> Bool> void populate(const NSL::Tensor<Type> & phi, Bool reshape);  // HubbardExp(SpinBasis)
```

The two changes need each other: with the old `populate(phi, bool)`, *every* matrix would satisfy both
concepts through the enum → `bool` conversion. Now a mismatched pairing is a compile error.

## The driver `autotune_RadialMCMC_PPP`

- `RadialHMC` with `PPPGaugeAction(V)` + `HubbardFermionAction<…, HubbardExp>`: charge basis only.
- `HMC: autotune: true` (default): the protocol of `autotune_RadialMCMC`, one trajectory per call into
  `/thermal`, `Nmd` read from the h5 file. `autotuner.py` works unchanged.
- `HMC: autotune: false`: a plain run with `Leapfrog: Nmd`, `HMC: Ntherm`, `HMC: Nconf` and an optional
  `HMC: seed`; rerunning on an existing file extends the chain.
- `Leapfrog: Fourier acceleration: true|false` selects the integrator (deck 4).
- Initial field from `S_gauge.sample()`; a warning for non-bipartite lattices (sign problem).
- Meta data: `/Meta/action = "PPP/hubbardExp"` and `/Meta/PPP/{form, V, …}`, so every ensemble records its
  interaction.
- Measurements: `Executables/Hubbard/propagator` with `measurements: basis: charge` (next slide).

`python/ppp_geometry.py` writes inputs for ideal benzenoids (benzene … perylene, coronene) with per-bond
hopping lists; `--bridge-hopping` rescales the two perylene bonds that join the naphthalene units.

## Measuring propagators: `Executables/Hubbard/propagator`

One program for both bases and both kinds of measurement (it replaces `propagatorChargeBasis` and
`propagatorSpinBasis`):

```yaml
measurements:
  basis: charge          # required: charge (HubbardExp, also PPP) or spin (HubbardExpSpinBasis)
  type: spatial          # spatial | momentum | both; default: momentum if wallSources are given
  Number Time Sources: 4
  wallSources: [...]     # momentum: blocks x bands x Nx entries [re, im]
stability: QR            # QR or SVD
```

`propagator -f run.yml [--config N] [--overwrite]`; results go into the ensemble file:

| path (under `<name>/`) | content |
|---|---|
| `markovChain/<n>/propagator/spatial/<species>/invM[t,s]`, `invM[s,t]`, `invM[t,t]` | position space, $(N_t,N_x,N_x)$ |
| `markovChain/<n>/propagator/momentum/<species>/invM[t,s]/<kSink>-<kSrc>` …, `Q` | all pairs of wall sources (each followed by its conjugate); $\frac1{N_t}\sum_t\operatorname{Tr}\,\mathrm{invM}[t,t]$ |
| `NonInteracting/propagator/{spatial,momentum}/…` | the same for $\phi=0$, $s=0$ |
| `Meta/propagator/basis`, `Meta/propagator/momentum/wallSources` | basis; the sources `kSink`, `kSrc` refer to |

[`<species>`: `particle`/`hole` or `spinUp`/`spinDown`; both bases measure the same quantities. The program refuses a basis that contradicts the
file, and wall sources that differ from those already used. Checked against exact inverses in both bases (deck 5, A10–A12).]{.small .muted}

## Tests: `Tests/Action/test_PPPGaugeAction.cpp`

9 test cases, 153 assertions, all pass.

| test case | catches |
|---|---|
| form names; matrix elements; interaction matrix from yml | wrong formula or units, parsing errors |
| on-site interaction reproduces `HubbardGaugeAction` ($U=3.7$) | normalization: $\delta$, factor $\frac12$ |
| two sites with non-integer $U=3.5$ against the analytic result | the integer truncation of $U$ |
| gauge force vs finite differences, and not aliased | sign or factor errors; shared buffers |
| invalid interaction matrices are rejected | non-symmetric or non-positive $V$ accepted silently |
| `sample()` draws $\phi_t\sim\mathcal N(0,\delta V)$ | wrong initial distribution |
| full action force (PPP gauge + charge-basis fermions) vs central finite differences, 4-site ring | the complete MD force |
